_about: The Evidence of Need register for all published AMU Business Problems and Techniques. This register is AMU's commitment to teaching only what can be evidenced (per QMS-020-08 section G). Each entry is grounded in an accreditation criterion, documented research, or lived experience. Curriculum-internal grounds are noted for transparency but do not substitute for external evidence.
standard: QMS-020-08 section G — The Evidence of Need Standard

units.title: Everything Depends on One Paycheque

grounds.ref: Sixth Annual Domestic Workers Report on Pay and Working Conditions for Domestic Workers in South Africa — SweepSouth, 2024
grounds.evidences: Documents that 84% of respondents are the sole breadwinner in their household, supporting an average of four dependents on one income — the real-world condition of an entire household resting on one paycheque.

grounds.ref: South Africa's unemployment rate rises to 32.7 percent — Hypertext, 2026 (Stats SA QLFS)
grounds.evidences: Shows one in three working-age South Africans has no job, meaning a single income earner's job loss routinely removes a household's only income with no readily available replacement.

units.title: Am I Building or in a Hole?
I Can't Say Where My Money Goes

grounds.ref: FinScope Consumer South Africa 2023/2024 — FinMark Trust
grounds.evidences: Shows living expenses consume about 85% of monthly income and 40% of adults borrow to buy food, evidencing that South African consumers manage tight, largely untracked cash flow where the total picture is easily lost.

units.title: My Income Stops the Moment I Stop Working
My Partner Controls Every Cent I Earn but I Cannot Access It
My Plan Keeps Breaking in the Same Place
The Economy Turned and Took My Plans with It

grounds.ref: Narrative attributions of entrepreneurial failure — Journal of Business Venturing (ScienceDirect), peer-reviewed
grounds.evidences: Peer-reviewed research on how entrepreneurs construct causal narratives after failure, attributing blame variably to themselves versus external/environmental factors, evidencing that mis-attributing the cause of a setback (self vs. circumstance) is a documented, real phenomenon among people who experience business failure.

units.title: My Savings Sit in the Bank Doing Nothing and Quietly Shrinking

grounds.ref: Inflation Calculator South Africa — CPI Buying Power Calculator, The Azanian Investor / Stats SA CPI data
grounds.evidences: Quantifies that R100 held in cash from the year 2000 buys only what roughly R27.65 could buy then in today's terms, evidencing that a headline sum of money left idle loses real value to inflation even though the number itself never falls.

grounds.ref: How does the latest CPI data affect you and your savings? — Moneyweb, 2024
grounds.evidences: Explains that money earning no interest is quietly losing value whenever CPI inflation exceeds the interest rate earned, directly evidencing the 'safe but shrinking' savings problem.

units.title: My Side Hustle Eats Time and Money but Never Proves Itself
One Bad Day Can Undo Years of Building

grounds.ref: 80% of South African homeowners are underinsured: Expert — SABC News, 2024
grounds.evidences: Reports that 80% of South African households are underinsured by close to 50% of their assets' true value, evidencing that most households have no adequate buffer against a single catastrophic loss such as fire.

units.title: I Keep Earning More and Owning No More
I Committed Before Verifying and Bought Someone Else's Problem
I Sign Up for Financial Products I Don't Understand

grounds.ref: Over-Indebtedness: National Treasury & National Credit Regulator — Parliamentary Monitoring Group (PMG), briefing on NCR data
grounds.evidences: Records National Credit Regulator findings that a large share of South Africa's 23 million+ credit-active consumers are impaired, evidencing a real, widespread pattern of credit agreements whose true total cost consumers did not grasp before signing.

units.title: No One Will Lend to Me When I Finally Need It

grounds.ref: Thin File Clients in South Africa's Financial Landscape — Eighty20, 2025
grounds.evidences: Documents the structural paradox that people 'need credit to build a credit history, yet lack the history required to access credit,' evidencing that being genuinely reliable but unable to produce visible proof of it is a real, named barrier facing millions of South Africans, especially the young, immigrants and gig workers.

units.title: The Instalment Looked Affordable, the Total Cost I Never Saw
Every Time I Get Ahead, Someone I Love Needs It More
Our Savings Club's Money Is Gone: A Year of Pooled Savings

grounds.ref: How to Protect Yourself From a Stokvel Scam — Franc, 2024
grounds.evidences: Documents recurring stokvel scams (e.g. the United African Stokvel case) and states plainly that 'there are no regulations on how and where mismanagement of stokvel funds is to be reported,' evidencing that pooled group savings concentrated in one person's control, with no external checks, is a real and recurring failure mode in South Africa.

units.title: Part of What I've Been Spending Was Never Mine
Skipping the Small Service Is How I Bought the Big One
The Betting App Gets Paid Before the Groceries Do

grounds.ref: South African's sport betting addiction: Calls to helpline soar 623% — Novanews (citing National Gambling Board / NRGP data), 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that problem gambling prevalence rose to 31% of the population (from under 6% in 2017) and that 32% of NRGP helpline callers cite financial difficulties from gambling, evidencing that a recurring outflow like gambling taking first claim on a household budget is a real and growing crisis in South Africa.

units.title: The Loan That Got Me Through the Month Now Owns My Months

grounds.ref: Over-Indebtedness: National Treasury & National Credit Regulator — Parliamentary Monitoring Group (PMG)
grounds.evidences: Documents that of over 23 million credit-active South African consumers, roughly 45% are classified impaired, evidencing that servicing multiple growing debt obligations until new resources go to old debt rather than new building is a widespread, real condition, not a rare one.

grounds.ref: Reckless Lending in South Africa — Your Rights Under the NCA — Debt Solutions 4U, 2026
grounds.evidences: Explains the National Credit Act's reckless-lending provisions, evidencing that South African law itself recognises and regulates against the real, common problem of borrowers being granted debt whose repayment burden outpaces their capacity to bear it.

units.title: The Message Looked Exactly Like My Bank, and My Savings Vanished

grounds.ref: South Africa Sees 86% Surge in Digital Banking Fraud, Losses Near R1.9 Billion — TechAfrica News, citing SABRIC 2025 Annual Banking Crime Statistics Report
grounds.evidences: Reports an 86% surge in digital banking fraud incidents (to nearly 98,000 cases, R1.888 billion in losses) driven primarily by social engineering — phishing followed by a vishing call impersonating the bank — directly evidencing the real, large-scale prevalence of exactly this scam pattern in South Africa.

units.title: The Money Owed to Me Isn't Here When My Bills Are

grounds.ref: Late Payments Are Affecting SMEs, Credit Data Shows — SME South Africa, 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that overdue business balances grew roughly 80% to R88.9 billion and that cash flow (not profit) is small businesses' single biggest threat when customers do not pay on time, evidencing the real phenomenon of being solvent over a period but short at the moment obligations fall due.

units.title: We've lived in this house for decades, but no paper says it's ours

grounds.ref: How many South Africans live in informal dwellings? And other home ownership stats — Superlinear, citing 2011 Census-derived land tenure research
grounds.evidences: Documents that nearly 60% of South Africans (around 30 million people) live on land or in dwellings held outside the formal title system — including RDP houses with untransferred titles and long-occupied backyard or communal land — evidencing that long possession and payment without a recognised title deed is a mass, real condition, not an isolated case.

units.title: Every generation in my family starts from zero

grounds.ref: Up to 70% of South Africans die without a valid Will, leaving families exposed to financial hardship — The Mercury / IOL, citing Discovery Life, 2026
grounds.evidences: Reports that up to 70% of South Africans die without a valid will, evidencing that unrecorded ownership of what a person has built is a real, majority-scale condition that leaves families' inheritance frozen or contested when the holder dies.

units.title: My earning power is real now, but I won't be able to afford to stop working

grounds.ref: Only 6% of South Africans can retire comfortably – are you one of them? — Moneyweb, citing 10X Investments Retirement Reality Report 2023/2024
grounds.evidences: Reports that only 6% of South Africans are on track to retire comfortably (receiving ~75% of final salary), with 72% of those off-track citing an inability to save enough — direct evidence that under-provisioning for a far-off retirement need, while feeling reasonable in the moment, is the dominant real-world outcome.

units.title: I'm forced to sell at the worst possible time

grounds.ref: Failure Of A Business In South Africa | Key Reasons Explored — JTB Consulting, 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that three in five South African business failures occur despite reported profits, because of timing mismatches and absent cash cushions, evidencing the real pattern of profitable, valuable-asset-holding operators being forced by a sudden shock into a distressed, discount sale for lack of liquid reserve.

units.title: My earning power has stopped growing
I am about to spend real money on demand I have only assumed
I have skills and encouragement but cannot choose which opportunity to pursue
I have launched but I cannot tell what the market is telling me
I keep adding features and never launch, and a real customer is waiting
Nobody is buying what we built
My product is good and my description is accurate, yet nobody switches
One fire, flood or looting spree and the business is gone

grounds.ref: 80% of South African homeowners are underinsured: Expert — SABC News, 2024
grounds.evidences: Establishes that 80% of South African households/asset-holders are underinsured by nearly half of their assets' true replacement value, evidencing that concentrated value with no adequate mechanism to absorb a single adverse event is the norm rather than the exception.

units.title: At my price and costs, the volume I need is a volume I can't reach
I am buying equipment and stock for demand that has not been confirmed

grounds.ref: Failure Of A Business In South Africa | Key Reasons Explored — JTB Consulting, 2025
grounds.evidences: Cites inadequate market validation and poor demand forecasting among the primary, documented causes of the 70-80% five-year SMME failure rate in South Africa, directly evidencing that committing money to equipment/stock ahead of confirmed demand is a common, costly real-world mistake.

units.title: No one will lend to us because the business is informal

grounds.ref: FinScope MSME South Africa 2024: Key findings — FinMark Trust, 2024
grounds.evidences: Reports that roughly 1.6 million MSMEs in South Africa operate informally (72% of micro-enterprises outside formal structures) and that 15% of MSME owners remain financially excluded, evidencing that operating genuinely and profitably without any independently legible record is a mass, real condition that blocks access to growth capital.

units.title: Stock keeps running out or expiring on the shelf
A formal opportunity is on the table and my unregistered business can't take it yet
Real prospects stall at 'let me think about it' and never come back
The people running this business are pulling in different directions
We grew faster than the business could carry

grounds.ref: Eskom hikes and rising fixed charges squeeze households and SMEs — Bizcommunity, 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that South African SMEs now face fixed monthly charges (up to R1,761 in Johannesburg) that apply regardless of how much they actually consume, directly evidencing the real phenomenon of unavoidable recurring costs outgrowing the surplus that current, real activity levels can cover.

units.title: A bigger, cheaper competitor moved into our market

grounds.ref: A qualitative study of the attitudes of South African spaza shop owners to coopetitive relationships — South African Journal of Business Management, peer-reviewed
grounds.evidences: Peer-reviewed study documenting that competition from larger, cheaper retail chains is ranked among the top external causes of township spaza shop failure, evidencing that a small operator being outmatched on price by a larger rival is a real, studied phenomenon in South Africa, not a hypothetical.

units.title: Compliance paperwork eats my margin every return, licence and renewal
Criminals demand a cut to let my business operate

grounds.ref: South Africa's construction mafia trains its sights on local government — Institute for Security Studies (ISS Africa), 2023
grounds.evidences: Documents that so-called 'business forums' demand a share (often described as '30%') of contract value as the price of being allowed to operate, with SAFCEC estimating at least R25.5 billion of construction projects violently disrupted, directly evidencing that extortion demands as the price of operating are a real, large-scale problem for South African businesses.

units.title: Customers Owe Us Money and Pay Whenever They Like
Customers Try It Once and Never Come Back
Everything Runs Through Me, I Cannot Hand the Work
I Can't Find, Afford or Keep the Skilled People My Business Needs

grounds.ref: These are the critical skills South Africa desperately needs in 2026 — BusinessTech, citing Department of Higher Education and Training National Scarce Skills List
grounds.evidences: Reports on the official National Scarce Skills List and documents shortages in fields such as engineering, artisanal trades, AI and cybersecurity, evidencing that businesses being unable to source, afford, or retain scarce skilled labour is a real, government-tracked condition in South Africa.

units.title: I Do Not Know How Much I Can Safely Pay Myself
My Business and Personal Money Are One Tangled Account
The Business Keeps Running Out of Cash Even Though It's Profitable
The Month Was Busy, the Customers Were Happy, and There's No Money
The Power Keeps Going Off, Every Outage Takes My Stock and Sales

grounds.ref: Estimating the economic cost of load shedding in South Africa — Nova Economics, 2023
grounds.evidences: Quantifies load shedding's cost to the South African economy at billions of rand (with manufacturing, transport, retail and agriculture bearing about 80% of the burden), directly evidencing that repeated, unpredictable failure of an externally supplied resource like power inflicts real, measurable, recurring damage on operators who depend on it.

units.title: The Work Is Good and Customers Are Happy, But Growth Has Stalled
There Is Nothing Between My Business and My Personal Life
We Sell the Asset When the Value Is in Selling the Outcome

grounds.ref: The Continuing Rise of Servitization in 2025: Embracing Outcome-Based Models — Copperberg, 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows that manufacturers are shifting revenue away from one-off product sales toward recurring outcome-based/servitized models, with revenue from outcome-based service models projected to grow from 25% to 41% over five years, evidencing that earning nothing between sales is a real and now widely-addressed commercial problem.

units.title: Our Assets and the Business Strategy Live in Different Worlds
The Pilot Impressed Everyone and Changed Nothing

grounds.ref: Shelfware Benchmark Report: The Cost of Software Waste — Vertice, 2025
grounds.evidences: Documents that a large share of enterprise software/technology licenses (industry estimates of 25-55%) go unused ('shelfware') after acquisition, evidencing that organisations repeatedly buy promising capabilities that are never woven into day-to-day work.

units.title: Nobody Has Agreed What Level of Service We Owe

grounds.ref: SERVQUAL Model of Service Quality — Toolshero (summarising Parasuraman, Zeithaml & Berry, 1988)
grounds.evidences: Confirms that, prior to structured gap-analysis models, service quality was widely acknowledged as abstract and not easily quantifiable/agreed upon, evidencing the real difficulty of settling what 'good service' means inside an organisation.

units.title: Nobody Pinned Down What the System Had to Do
We Can't Economically Get Trustworthy Data Off Our Assets

grounds.ref: Cisco Survey Reveals Close to Three-Fourths of IoT Projects Are Failing — Cisco Newsroom, 2017
grounds.evidences: Reports that 60% of IoT initiatives stall at the proof-of-concept stage and about 74% fail overall, citing integration, data-quality and budget-overrun challenges — evidencing that chaining sensing, power, connectivity and trust into one working asset-monitoring system is a genuine, widespread failure point, not a theoretical one.

units.title: We Keep Getting Blindsided by People Who Can Stop Us

grounds.ref: Pulse of the Profession 2026: Driving Success in Complex Projects — PMI, 2026 (summarised by pmwares)
grounds.evidences: Shows that 31% of complex projects now fail to achieve their intended benefits (more than double the prior rate), and that high-performing teams differ specifically by earlier, phased stakeholder engagement — evidencing that being stopped late by unanticipated stakeholders is a real and measured driver of project failure.

units.title: We Keep Getting the Future Wrong: Capacity Shortfalls or Waste

grounds.ref: Stanford Graduate School of Business (2004). Whang and Lee: Eliminating the Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains — summarizing Lee, Padmanabhan & Whang (1997), 'The Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains,' Sloan Management Review
grounds.evidences: Documents that demand-information distortion moving upstream through a supply chain systematically causes both insufficient and excessive capacity at once (plants 'scramble to accommodate beginning-of-the-month orders, then lie idle for weeks'), directly evidencing that sizing capacity off the last shock rather than real demand is a documented, named industrial phenomenon, not just this unit's own experience.

units.title: We're Planning Year to Year While Our Commitments Span Decades

grounds.ref: Report cards, and other tracking of South Africa's public sector fixed infrastructure condition — SAICE/scielo.org.za, 2024
grounds.evidences: Documents South Africa's SAICE infrastructure report card decline to a D grade by 2022, driven explicitly by chronic under-funding of maintenance against long-horizon needs (e.g. Eskom's 'keep the lights on' short-termism), evidencing that large predictable long-horizon costs are routinely deferred by short annual budget cycles until failure occurs.

units.title: Every Site Manages Assets Its Own Way, There Is No Learning
Every Subsystem Met Its Spec and the System Still Failed

grounds.ref: Wikipedia, citing NASA Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report (1999)
grounds.evidences: Documents a real, famous case in which every subsystem supplied by NASA and by contractor Lockheed Martin passed its own internal verification, yet the spacecraft was destroyed because the two correctly-functioning components used different unit systems at the interface — with NASA's own associate administrator stating the failure was 'not the error; it was the failure of NASA's systems engineering... to detect the error' — evidencing that integration failure despite component-level correctness is a documented, attributed systemic-responsibility problem, not a fluke.

grounds.ref: NASA Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board (1999). Phase I Report
grounds.evidences: The primary NASA investigation-board document establishing that the root cause was a ground-software interface specification mismatch between two correctly-tested systems, corroborating that the failure was one of integration and systems engineering rather than any single component's fault.

units.title: Our Assets Were Designed for a Climate That No Longer Exists

grounds.ref: How to make infrastructure more resilient against climate change — ASCE Civil Engineering Source, 2022
grounds.evidences: States plainly that the 'stationarity' assumption baked into engineering design codes and standards is no longer valid because climate is no longer stable, so infrastructure built correctly to historical assumptions now fails more often under conditions it was never designed for.

units.title: Our model of the asset doesn't match reality, so we can't trust its decisions

grounds.ref: A Continual Validation, Updating, and Decision-Making Framework for Self-Adaptive Digital Twins via Robust Model Predictive Control — arXiv, 2026
grounds.evidences: States that static asset/process models 'drift out of alignment' with the real thing through parameter variation, unmodeled dynamics and degradation, and that model-based decisions depend critically on the model staying synchronised with reality — evidencing the exact risk of trusting a frozen model of a since-repaired or worn asset.

units.title: Our new assets arrive with their problems built in
Our safety and control systems are one fault or one breach from failing

grounds.ref: TRITON Malware Remains Threat to Global Critical Infrastructure — CISA/FBI/NSA Joint Cybersecurity Advisory, IC3, 2022
grounds.evidences: Confirms a real, documented case (TRITON/TRISIS) in which attackers moved laterally from a shared IT/OT network onto a plant's safety instrumented system and installed malware capable of disabling or manipulating it — evidencing that automated last-line-of-defence systems can genuinely be both unreliable when frozen in place and reachable by attackers.

units.title: Our smart infrastructure has to serve a whole city, not just its parts
Our sustainability promises and our asset decisions live in different worlds

grounds.evidences: Reports that only around 20% of chief procurement officers use sustainability measures as a primary criterion in sourcing decisions and fewer than 10% embed it in category strategies, evidencing a real, measured gap between an organisation's public sustainability commitment and its everyday purchasing decisions.

units.title: Structures fail suddenly under cyclic loads we didn't design for

grounds.ref: What is Metal Fatigue? An Overview — YENA Engineering
grounds.evidences: States that over 90% of mechanical failures are caused by metal fatigue rather than a single overload event, evidencing that a component clearing a one-off static-load check can still fail catastrophically from repeated cyclic loading, exactly as in the cracked weld case.

units.title: We can't quantify whole-system production availability

grounds.ref: System Reliability & Availability Calculations — BMC Software Blog
grounds.evidences: Shows with a worked example that a series-connected system's availability is the multiplied product of its components' individual availabilities, not an average — e.g. two 99%-available components in series yield only 98.01% — evidencing that summing/eyeballing subsystem numbers as 'good enough' genuinely understates whole-system risk.

units.title: We can't systematically find and size the hazards before they hurt us

grounds.ref: What is the difference between a trial and a pilot? — Association for Project Management (APM)
grounds.evidences: States that pilots/trials exist specifically to let an organisation identify deficiencies and manage the risk of a new method before substantial resources are committed, evidencing that committing real time and money to an unproven method without first testing it is a recognised, addressable risk in project practice.

units.title: We can't value flexibility - when to defer, expand or abandon

grounds.ref: Why Are Megaprojects, Including Nuclear Power Plants, Delivered Overbudget and Late? Reasons and Remedies — Flyvbjerg, arXiv preprint, 2018
grounds.evidences: Documents (via Flyvbjerg's large-sample megaproject research) that roughly 90% of megaprojects run over budget, driven by single-point forecasts and optimism bias that ignore the ability to wait, phase or stop — evidencing that basing a large hard-to-reverse commitment on one fixed forecast is a genuine, repeated cause of costly failure.

units.title: Capital decisions are made on purchase price, and we pay for it for years

grounds.ref: Understanding Total Cost of Ownership in Construction Fleets — Construction Executive
grounds.evidences: Explains that purchase price is only one part of an equipment cost equation dominated by financing, maintenance, repairs, fuel and downtime, and that an asset that looks affordable at purchase can become the most expensive in the fleet — directly evidencing the 'cheapest bakkie could be the most expensive' claim.

units.title: Every variation becomes a claim, and every claim becomes a fight
I'm being pressured to sign what I shouldn't - the tender, the inspection, the certificate

grounds.ref: Accountants' ethics under pressure — ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants), 2022
grounds.evidences: Reports survey data that 27% of accounting professionals had been put under pressure in the prior three years to act unethically — including downplaying risk in plans and forecasts — evidencing that being pressured to attach one's sign-off to something untrue or unsafe is a real, measured workplace experience, not a hypothetical.

units.title: Our spares are priced in dollars and our revenue is in rand

grounds.ref: Rand volatility poses significant risks for South African SMEs in global trade — Business Report, 2026
grounds.evidences: Reports that a 3-5% rand move between order and settlement can wipe out an SME's profit entirely, and that most South African trading businesses operate without a formal foreign-exchange strategy, evidencing that essential recurring costs floating on an uncontrolled external price genuinely rewrites operating plans.

units.title: The business case was one confident number, and reality blew through it

grounds.ref: Why Are Megaprojects, Including Nuclear Power Plants, Delivered Overbudget and Late? Reasons and Remedies — Flyvbjerg, arXiv preprint, 2018
grounds.evidences: Identifies optimism bias and strategic misrepresentation — confident, precise forecasts produced by parties whose interest is in the forecast being accepted rather than being accurate — as the two primary, empirically documented causes of megaproject cost/schedule overrun, evidencing that trusting a single confident number is a real, repeated decision failure.

units.title: We bought the assets before we understood them

grounds.ref: Seven Common M&A Due Diligence Pitfalls — Miller Cooper, 2024
grounds.evidences: States that buyers who skip on-site inspection and rely only on the seller's financials can miss old, obsolete or damaged equipment and inventory that a balance sheet alone will not reveal, directly evidencing acquisitions judged on financial output while the physical condition of the underlying asset goes unexamined.

units.title: We decide big asset spend on price and gut feel, and can't defend it

grounds.ref: Understanding Total Cost of Ownership in Construction Fleets — Construction Executive
grounds.evidences: Shows that decision-makers who compare long-lived assets on purchase price alone systematically misjudge which option is cheaper to own, because financing, maintenance, fuel and downtime dominate lifecycle cost — evidencing that asset-spend decisions made on price/gut feel and not total cost of ownership are a real, documented failure pattern.

units.title: We fitted parts from a seller we can't even call back
We've outsourced the work but kept the risk
Projects hand over new assets that operations can't run

grounds.ref: Asset Information Handover Guidelines from Planning and Construction to Operations and Maintenance — National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (Transportation Research Board), 2024
grounds.evidences: States directly that receiving a constructed asset and closeout documentation 'does not mean that the organization has achieved operational readiness,' and documents recurring failures to plan handover requirements (records, documentation, spares, training) before construction begins — evidencing that a signed-off handover is routinely mistaken for a genuinely operable asset.

units.title: A cyber attack can now stop the plant - our control systems are wide open

grounds.ref: SANS 2024 ICS/OT Cybersecurity Survey Reveals Significant Progress While Highlighting That Major Gaps Remain in Securing Critical Infrastructure — SANS Institute, 2024
grounds.evidences: Reports that many organisations still lack central governance for industrial cyber risk management and dedicated incident-response planning for ICS/OT, evidencing the real-world gap where neither IT nor engineering fully owns the security of the computers and networks that now run critical physical operations.

units.title: A key customer is auditing us and we can't show them we're in control

grounds.ref: Nurcahyo, Zulfadlillah & Habiburrahman (2021). Relationship between ISO 9001:2015 and operational and business performance of manufacturing industries in a developing country — Heliyon
grounds.evidences: A peer-reviewed study of 50 manufacturers found ISO 9001 variables explained only 31.6-35% of variance in business/operational performance, and separately documented major implementation barriers (personnel competency, weak management commitment) — evidencing that certification and demonstrated operational capability are empirically only loosely coupled, so 'passing the audit' and 'running a good shop' are measurably different things worth distinguishing rather than conflating.

units.title: A thousand alarms a shift, and the one that matters gets lost

grounds.ref: Avoiding the high risk of alarm floods — EEMUA, 2024
grounds.evidences: EEMUA's own guidance body states that alarm floods cause 'control room operator overload, known to be a frequent factor in industrial disasters', directly evidencing that flooded warning channels train operators to miss the alarm that matters.

grounds.ref: Alarm Management by the Numbers — Emerson, industry alarm performance data
grounds.evidences: Documents a real 12-hour incident with 3,712 alarms (over 300/hour) whose volume caused delays and errors in responding to the alarms that were genuinely critical, evidencing the false-alarm-flood problem at the heart of this unit.

units.title: Asset management is seen as the maintenance department's job alone
Asset risks only surface after they've hurt us

grounds.ref: Recurrent Audit Findings and Organizational Culture — Internal Auditor (IIA), April 2026
grounds.evidences: Documents that known risks noted informally ('quiet worries', unowned action items) recur because they never become a governed, owned, dated commitment — the exact 'we saw it coming' failure pattern this unit targets, generalised across audited organisations.

units.title: Critical machines fail without warning because we can't see inside them

grounds.ref: Prediction at scale: How industry can get more value out of maintenance — McKinsey & Company
grounds.evidences: McKinsey's operations research finds predictive/condition-based maintenance (reading a machine's ongoing signals) typically cuts downtime 30-50% and extends machine life 20-40% versus inspecting only when stopped or broken, evidencing the real cost of blindness between scheduled checks.

units.title: Every department hit its targets and the whole strategy still failed
Everything is marked urgent - we can't tell which jobs actually matter
Findings get raised and then forgotten - corrective actions never land

grounds.ref: Culture Problems Behind Recurrent Audit Findings — Internal Auditor (Institute of Internal Auditors), April 2026
grounds.evidences: The IIA's own practitioner literature confirms recurring findings are the norm where organisations lack a structured recurrence-tracking/closure process, and that vague ownership and unenforced deadlines are the specific mechanism — directly evidencing this unit's 'we keep fixing the same problems' pattern.

units.title: Half the instruments are out of calibration - we run on numbers we can't trust

grounds.ref: Bartel, T. NIST (2016). 'Uncertainty in NIST Force Measurements' — PMC
grounds.evidences: A national metrology institute's own peer-reviewed uncertainty analysis shows that even NIST's reference-grade force instruments carry quantified uncertainty and require cross-checking multiple transducers against each other to detect drift, evidencing that disagreement between two instruments measuring the same physical quantity is an expected, documented metrology problem requiring a formal method to resolve — not a sign either gauge is simply 'broken.'

units.title: If disaster struck tomorrow, we'd be improvising
Investigations turn into blame, so people stop telling us the truth

grounds.ref: The Swiss Cheese Model of Accident Causation — James Reason (1990), summarised via OERCollective WHS/HR guide
grounds.evidences: Reason's widely-adopted model, developed specifically to counter blame-focused investigation, evidences that the person at the 'sharp end' typically sits in front of organisational/latent conditions (training, tools, procedures) that investigation-by-blame leaves untouched, so the same failure recurs under a different name.

units.title: Jobs grow once the covers come off - scope creep blindsides the budget
Jobs start without a proper scope - the crew arrives unready
Large structures degrade where we can't inspect them

grounds.ref: Bridge Infrastructure Problems in the US — ASCE 2025 Infrastructure Report Card
grounds.evidences: ASCE's national bridge data shows over 46,000 US bridges are structurally deficient and that funding gaps leave deterioration and access-limited inspection backlogs unresolved for years, evidencing the real-world prevalence of the exact dilemma (an inaccessible pier, an inspection that cannot reach the whole structure, deferred close inspection) this unit dramatises.

units.title: Machines wear out far faster than they should and we don't know why

grounds.ref: Prediction at scale: How industry can get more value out of maintenance — McKinsey & Company
grounds.evidences: McKinsey documents that nearly half of industrial maintenance activity remains reactive (swap/reset without analysing failure mode), evidencing that repeatedly replacing a failing part without diagnosing how it actually fails is a widespread, costly real-world pattern rather than a hypothetical one.

units.title: Nobody can say whether our assets are performing

grounds.ref: What asset management maturity assessments miss on asset performance — Optimal (drawing on IAM/ISO 55001 maturity research)
grounds.evidences: Documents that widely-used asset management maturity assessments (aligned to ISO 55001) measure whether governance processes exist, not whether the assets actually perform well — evidencing that organisations can and do lack any honest, agreed measure of 'are we actually doing well', exactly as this unit describes.

units.title: Nobody is clearly responsible for this asset - everyone assumed someone else was
Nobody knows what the asset base is actually worth
Nothing lines up on the day - crew, parts, permit and access never align
Our assets are being stolen and stripped faster than we can repair them

grounds.ref: Ripple effects — new report unpacks the corrosive scourge of copper cable theft in South Africa — Daily Maverick, citing Global Initiative Against Transnational Organised Crime, 2023
grounds.evidences: Reports that Transnet, Prasa and Eskom alone logged almost 11,000 cable-theft incidents a year (2018-2022) at a direct cost of roughly R7 billion annually and R187 billion in wider economic ripple effects, evidencing that infrastructure asset owners face a deliberate, adaptive, repeat-attacking adversary rather than accidental loss — the exact real-world condition this unit addresses.

units.title: Our job estimates are guesses - durations and crew sizes are pulled from thin air
Our maintenance strategies and task lists are built on guesswork, not evidence

grounds.ref: Prediction at scale: How industry can get more value out of maintenance — McKinsey & Company
grounds.evidences: McKinsey's finding that nearly half of maintenance is still reactive despite organisations believing they run preventive programmes evidences the real cost of maintenance plans not built from genuine failure data, which is the trap this unit describes.

units.title: Our own maintenance keeps introducing the next failure

grounds.ref: Reliabilityweb (Uptime Elements). 'Root Cause Analysis' — industry reliability-engineering reference
grounds.evidences: States that root cause failure analysis (RCFA) exists specifically because fixes that address only the immediate/apparent cause allow the same failure to recur, and that RCA/RCFA is the documented discipline for finding the deeper cause — evidencing that 'properly fixed but keeps breaking' is a recognised category of maintenance failure with an established diagnostic response, not evidence the repair itself is being done carelessly.

units.title: Our waste leaves the site the cheapest way and comes back as a disaster
Preventive maintenance keeps slipping - service dates pass and the routine work never gets called

grounds.ref: Prediction at scale: How industry can get more value out of maintenance — McKinsey & Company
grounds.evidences: McKinsey's operations research documents that the majority of manufacturers' maintenance activity slips into reactive mode despite having planned schedules, consistent with this unit's claim that correct plan dates alone do not prevent work from lapsing without a working 'ready-to-do' pipeline.

units.title: Some assets stand idle while others are run past their limit

grounds.ref: Asset Utilization 101: Identify Underused Equipment and Right-size — ClearPathGPS fleet-utilization industry analysis
grounds.evidences: Documents that fleets routinely carry both overused assets (utilisation above 85-90%, driving premature wear and breakdowns) and underused assets (drawing the same insurance/maintenance/financing costs without matching output), evidencing exactly the mismatch between raw activity and true capacity this unit targets.

units.title: Someone Got Hurt by the Hazard We All Walked Past

grounds.ref: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (2006). 'CSB Investigation of BP Texas City Refinery Disaster Continues as Organizational Issues Are Probed'
grounds.evidences: A federal investigation agency's own findings state that internal BP documents from 2002-2005 showed the company knew of significant safety problems at Texas City and 34 other business units months or years before the March 2005 explosion that killed 15 workers, evidencing with a documented, high-consequence real case that a hazard being 'on the list' does not by itself change outcomes — the gap between known risk and acted-upon risk is a real, investigated organisational failure mode.

units.title: The Alarms Are Bypassed, the Interlocks Overridden

grounds.ref: CSB investigation into 2019 PES refinery fire and explosion, Philadelphia — reported via WHYY, 2022
grounds.evidences: The US Chemical Safety Board found that a corroded pipe required inspection under both OSHA and EPA rules that never occurred, that remote emergency isolation valves were never installed, and that emergency water suppression failed — a stack of independently-permitted safeguard gaps, each individually explainable, that combined to allow a catastrophic HF release; this evidences how layered safety systems really do get quietly eroded decision by decision.

units.title: The Asset Management System Itself Is Never Reviewed

grounds.ref: Culture Problems Behind Recurrent Audit Findings — Internal Auditor (Institute of Internal Auditors), April 2026
grounds.evidences: Documents that the same audit findings reappear cycle after cycle because the information raised in a report is never fed back into the incentives, budgets or rules that actually govern behaviour — evidencing this unit's pattern of warnings reaching a record but never travelling back into governing rules.

units.title: The Asset Register Can't Be Trusted (Register History)
The Backlog Keeps Growing and Nobody Knows What's Real

grounds.ref: U.S. Government Accountability Office (2025). 'Federal Real Property: Disposing of Unneeded Facilities Could Help Reduce Maintenance Backlog' (GAO-25-108400)
grounds.evidences: Documents that the U.S. federal government's own building deferred-maintenance backlog more than doubled from $171 billion to $370 billion between FY2017 and FY2024, and separately flags that agencies struggle to reliably report and communicate the size of that backlog to Congress — evidencing both that maintenance backlogs only grow when deferred and that even large, resourced organisations cannot trust their own backlog counts.

units.title: The Drawings and Records Don't Match What's Actually There
The Job Is Ready but the Parts Aren't (Stockouts)

grounds.ref: MRO and Spare Parts Inventory Statistics — Reliamag, citing SPARETECH 2025 survey of 300 manufacturing executives and Plant Engineering 2025 Maintenance Survey
grounds.evidences: Reports that 23% of unplanned downtime events are directly attributable to unavailable spare parts and that 32% of operations leaders face frequent stockouts of critical parts, evidencing that planned work stalling on a part that fails to arrive in time is a widespread, measured real-world failure, not a hypothetical.

units.title: The Maintenance Budget Is Last Year Plus Inflation
The Master Data Doesn't Match the Plant Equipment
The Parts Are Never There When We Need Them, or Cash Is Frozen When We Don't

grounds.ref: MRO and Spare Parts Inventory Statistics — Reliamag, citing SPARETECH 2025 survey of 300 manufacturing executives
grounds.evidences: Documents the exact 'buried in spares yet caught short' paradox: 32% of operations leaders report frequent stockouts of critical parts while 22% of MRO inventory sits unused for over five years and 48% cite high inventory spend as a top challenge — evidencing that managing spares as one undifferentiated lump (rather than by consequence and demand) produces simultaneous shortage and waste in real organisations.

units.title: The Plan Assumes People, Skills and Structures We Don't Have

grounds.ref: The Talent Shortage Crippling South Africa Is in the Trades, Not in Tech — Engineering News, 2026
grounds.evidences: Reports that the share of South African companies struggling to recruit artisans more than doubled from 10% (2024) to 22% (2025), with maintenance-engineer shortages surging to 38%, and that TVET throughput sits at only 14% — evidencing that plans assuming trained technicians and engineers exist 'on the ground' routinely collide with a real, worsening national capability gap, exactly as this unit describes.

units.title: The Planner Can't Get Anyone to Commit (Operations)
The Planner's Own Day Is Consumed by Firefighting
The Plant Gets Changed Without Anyone Controlling the Records

grounds.ref: Cost Analysis of Inadequate Interoperability in the U.S. Capital Facilities Industry — NIST GCR 04-867, Gallaher et al., 2004
grounds.evidences: This NIST-published study quantified $15.8 billion in annual US costs from inadequate interoperability of facility data, two-thirds borne by owners/operators, directly evidencing that drift between a system's real, as-built state and its recorded drawings/registers is a real, large, measured cost — not a hypothetical inconvenience.

units.title: The Procedure on the Wall Isn't the Way We Actually Work

grounds.ref: Aligning work-as-imagined and work-as-done using FRAM on a hospital ward: a roadmap — PMC (peer-reviewed), 2022
grounds.evidences: This peer-reviewed study, built on Hollnagel's Safety-II framework, documents the routine, real-world gap between the officially written procedure ('work-as-imagined') and what skilled staff actually do to get the job done ('work-as-done') in complex operational settings, evidencing exactly the split this unit dramatises between the fictional paper process and the real unwritten practice.

units.title: The Same Failures Keep Coming Back - We Fix the Symptom

grounds.ref: Wang, S-H. et al., 'Failure Analysis and Prevention of Extraction Column for Methyl Methacrylate Production: Application of the Safety Design Concept' — Materials (MDPI/PMC), 2021
grounds.evidences: Traces a real recurring equipment wear failure to root causes in design, manufacturing and installation that kept reproducing the same symptom until proactive root-cause elimination (rather than repeated remedial fixes) was applied — the exact trap in this unit.

units.title: The Schedule Keeps Being Broken by Emergent Work

grounds.ref: 'Maintenance practices that drive site performance' — McKinsey & Company
grounds.evidences: Documents a real site where schedule compliance (the measured gap between planned and actual maintenance work) sat at an unmeasured 70% baseline until it was tracked and systematically closed to 95%, showing the gap is real, common, and invisible until measured.

units.title: The Shutdown Always Overruns - Hundreds of Interdependent Tasks
The Way We Operate the Equipment Is Destroying It

grounds.ref: NIST/SEMATECH (2012). e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §8.1.2.4 'Bathtub curve'
grounds.evidences: A U.S. federal standards-body statistical reference documents the 'Early Failure Period,' also called the Infant Mortality Period, as a distinct, well-characterised phase of elevated early-life failure rate distinct from wear-out failure — evidencing that components dying young after passing initial checks is a formally recognised reliability-engineering pattern with its own name and cause structure (defects, installation, handling), not a mysterious run of bad luck.

units.title: We Can't Find the Right Document When We Need It
We Can't Name the Skills Our Assets Need

grounds.ref: GFMAM, 'Competency Specification for an ISO 55001 Asset Management System Assessor', 1st Edition v2 — Global Forum on Maintenance and Asset Management / The IAM
grounds.evidences: The global professional body for asset management has had to formally publish task-level competency specifications precisely because organisations otherwise hire and train by job title without ever writing down what each role must actually know and do.

units.title: We Can't Predict When Our Assets Will Fail

grounds.ref: Reliabilityweb. 'Repair vs. Replace: How to Use Lifecycle Cost Analysis to Determine the Threshold Limit'
grounds.evidences: Sets out a documented lifecycle-cost-analysis method (comparing net present value of 'buy new' versus 'keep and maintain' options to derive a maintenance-cost multiplier threshold) specifically because ad hoc replace decisions are unreliable — evidencing that a defensible, asset-specific 'replace it now' number is a real, calculable output of an established method rather than something that has to be guessed or benchmarked from someone else's number.

units.title: We Can't Say Which Assets Matter Most

grounds.ref: Palmer, R.D. (Doc Palmer), Machinery Lubrication / Reliable Plant. 'The What, Why and How of Wrench Time'
grounds.evidences: Written by the author of the Maintenance Planning and Scheduling Handbook, states that documented wrench-time studies across industry consistently find technicians spend only 25-35% of their shift on hands-on tool work, with the rest lost to travel, waiting, and searching — evidencing that being 'busy all day on the wrong things' is a measured, industry-wide planning-and-scheduling gap, not this particular crew's discipline problem.

units.title: We Can't Show Stakeholders or the Auditors What the Assets Delivered
We Can't Tell Whether a Critical Component Is Cracking Inside

grounds.ref: 'Liquid Penetrant Testing: An Essential Method for NDT Inspections' — American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT)
grounds.evidences: The industry standards body for nondestructive testing states plainly that 'PT [penetrant testing] cannot reveal discontinuities that are not open to the part surface' — confirming that a clean dye-penetrant result on a thick weld is genuinely silent about anything growing beneath the surface.

units.title: We Found a Flaw and Can't Say Whether It's Safe to Keep Running

grounds.ref: 'What is Fitness-for-Service (FFS) in Engineering? API 579 Explained with Examples' — IDEA Metrics Global Engineering
grounds.evidences: Describes the real, codified API 579/ASME FFS-1 engineering methodology that exists specifically to replace the crude 'shut down vs hope' binary with a disciplined, data-driven run/repair/replace/monitor decision for equipment found with an in-service flaw.

units.title: We Have Asset Data but Can't Turn It into Reliable Decisions

grounds.ref: 'Frequency–Severity Asymmetry and Regime-Based Forecasting of Operational Downtime in Continuous Material-Handling Systems' — Mathematics (MDPI), 2026
grounds.evidences: Analysing 6,605 real industrial failure events, the study finds strong disproportionality between raw failure frequency and actual downtime burden — direct evidence that the 'obvious number' (how often something happens) systematically misleads decisions about what actually matters.

units.title: We Inspect What's Easy on a Calendar, the Degradation Happens Where We Never Look

grounds.ref: DNV (2021). 'Terminology Explained: What is Risk-Based Inspection (RBI)?' — explainer of API RP 580/581
grounds.evidences: Explains that RBI methodology exists because a large share of total unit risk concentrates in a small percentage of equipment items, so routine/uniform inspection frequencies do not target where damage is actually likely to occur — evidencing that a huge volume of inspections following a fixed plan can still miss the specific location where failure originates, which is precisely why the risk-based, consequence-weighted alternative was developed industry-wide.

units.title: We Made This Month's Numbers by Borrowing from the Tax We Owe
We Maintain on a Calendar, Not on Condition
We Only Find Out We're Failing When the Auditor or Customer Tells Us

grounds.evidences: Documents the 'watermelon effect' as a named, recognised pattern where internal SLA/KPI metrics show green (targets met) while the people actually experiencing the service report red (frustration, dissatisfaction) because the metrics measure technical/operational proxies rather than the experience customers actually have — evidencing that a quality report that is 'a sea of green' can coexist with real, undetected customer-facing failure by documented mechanism, not coincidence.

units.title: When Experienced People Leave, What They Know Walks Out With Them

grounds.ref: '2.1 Million Manufacturing Jobs Could Go Unfilled by 2030' — National Association of Manufacturers, citing Deloitte & The Manufacturing Institute study, 2021
grounds.evidences: Documents a severe, growing, industry-wide shortage of experienced skilled workers (finding qualified workers 36% harder than in 2018) — the exact real-world vulnerability this unit describes when an organisation's operating knowledge lives in one person who can leave.

units.title: When the Primary Failed, the Standby Failed Too

grounds.ref: Mateus, R.J.G. et al., 'An Integrated Risk-Informed Multicriteria Approach for Determining Optimal Inspection Periods for Protective Sensors' — Sensors (MDPI/PMC), 2025
grounds.evidences: States that hidden (dormant) failures 'can account for up to half of all failure modes' in protective/standby equipment, remaining undetected until a real demand exposes them — direct evidence that backups can fail silently exactly as described in this unit.

units.title: Work Gets Done but Never Closed Out - Open Work Orders Pile Up
Work Requests Arrive Vague, Duplicated or Wrong
Disposal Is an Afterthought and the Dead Asset's Duties Live On

grounds.ref: 'How to Account for Decommissioning Provision under IFRS' — CPDbox (IAS 37 / IAS 16 analysis)
grounds.evidences: Confirms that an obligation to remove/restore an asset arises the moment it is built and continues regardless of whether it is still in use — evidencing that a thing's obligations genuinely do not stop when people simply stop using it.

units.title: Ribbon-Cuttings Win Votes, Maintenance Wins Nothing

grounds.ref: 'Private sector urged to plug funding gap in infrastructure development' — SAnews (South African Government News Agency), 13 May 2026, citing Deputy Minister of Finance David Masondo
grounds.evidences: Reports a real, government-acknowledged R36 billion annual municipal infrastructure maintenance gap in South Africa, evidencing that upkeep of existing infrastructure is chronically underfunded relative to the visible new-build spending it competes against.

units.title: The Renewal Backlog Is Growing Faster Than the Money

grounds.ref: 'Private sector urged to plug funding gap in infrastructure development' — SAnews (South African Government News Agency), 13 May 2026
grounds.evidences: The formally estimated R36 billion annual municipal infrastructure maintenance shortfall in South Africa evidences a real, quantified, growing gap between what a collection of ageing assets needs to stay in good repair and what money is actually available — precisely the funding-prioritisation dilemma this unit addresses.

units.title: Unused Spares and Repairable Components Get Dumped as Scrap

grounds.ref: Russell, J.D. & Nasr, N.Z., 'Value-retained vs. impacts avoided: the differentiated contributions of remanufacturing, refurbishment, repair, and reuse within a circular economy' — Journal of Remanufacturing (Springer), 2022/2023
grounds.evidences: Peer-reviewed analysis quantifying that reuse, repair, refurbishment and remanufacturing retain substantially more economic and material value than disposal — evidencing that organisations which default to discarding usable or restorable items are destroying real, recoverable value.

units.title: We Can't Prove Whether to Repair, Rebuild or Replace
Our Infrastructure Projects Stall on Local Content and Community Obligations
Our Strategy Is Brittle - One Shock Could Break It

grounds.ref: Cao, Y., Dong, Y., Ma, D., & Sun, L. (2021). Customer concentration and corporate risk-taking. Journal of Financial Stability, 54, 100890
grounds.evidences: This peer-reviewed study documents that firms with a small number of large customers face materially higher cash-flow uncertainty and risk exposure tied to losing any one of them, providing empirical grounding that a single cancelled contract representing the bulk of a business's revenue is a well-documented structural failure mode, not a freak event.

units.title: My Investments Are All in One Basket and I Am Terrified

grounds.ref: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2024). 34.7 percent of business establishments born in 2013 were still operating in 2023. Business Employment Dynamics
grounds.evidences: Official U.S. government longitudinal data show that fewer than half of new business establishments survive even five years, and the steepest survival-rate drop happens in the very first year of operation, evidencing that the fragility of a hard-built small business to a single bad turn is a broad, government-measured pattern rather than an isolated misfortune.

units.title: We Are Growing Fast but the Culture Is Breaking Apart

grounds.ref: Wasserman, N. (2003). Founder-CEO Succession and the Paradox of Entrepreneurial Success. Organization Science, 14(2), 149-172
grounds.evidences: Wasserman's award-winning empirical study of founder-led companies finds that the more successfully a founder scales a company, the more likely that founder (and, by extension, the founding culture and practices) is to be displaced by professionalizing pressures, evidencing that the erosion of what made a growing organisation good, and the exit of the people who built it, is a documented structural consequence of scaling rather than a leadership failure alone.

units.title: We Need to Raise Our Next Round and Cannot Build a Defensible Valuation

grounds.ref: Puri, M., & Zarutskie, R. (2012). On the Life Cycle Dynamics of Venture-Capital- and Non-Venture-Capital-Financed Firms. Journal of Finance, 67(6), 2247-2293 (NBER Working Paper No. 14250)
grounds.evidences: Using two decades of U.S. firm-level data, this study documents that early-stage ventures' survival and growth trajectories are highly uncertain and diverge sharply over time, underscoring why standard valuation methods built on predictable cash flows fail for early-stage companies and why founders raising a next round genuinely struggle to construct a defensible valuation from thin, volatile evidence.

units.title: Our Decommissioning Plan Is a Huge Unfunded Liability

grounds.ref: 'How to Account for Decommissioning Provision under IFRS' — CPDbox (IAS 37 / IAS 16 analysis)
grounds.evidences: Explains that under IAS 37/IAS 16 a decommissioning liability must be recognised at present value from the day the asset is built, precisely because failing to do so would let reported profits over the asset's life quietly overstate reality while the real future cost goes unfunded — the exact mechanism this unit describes.

units.title: We are throwing away waste that our competitors turn into money

grounds.ref: Russell, J.D. & Nasr, N.Z., 'Value-retained vs. impacts avoided: the differentiated contributions of remanufacturing, refurbishment, repair, and reuse within a circular economy' — Journal of Remanufacturing (Springer), 2022/2023
grounds.evidences: Quantifies the differentiated economic value retained by reuse, repair, refurbishment and remanufacturing versus disposal — direct evidence that end-of-life items routinely carry recoverable value that a competitor could capture while the discarding party pays disposal costs for it instead.

units.title: Our investors and regulators demand ESG data we don't have

grounds.ref: Bogdanov, A., 'South Africa's ESG data can be a new operating system for the future of business' — Africa at LSE (London School of Economics), 26 November 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that only around 30% of JSE-listed companies disclose emissions, just 21% report Scope 3 emissions, only 30% report water usage and 11% recycling — evidencing that most South African operations' systems are genuinely unready to produce the audited carbon/water/injury figures increasingly demanded by banks and regulators.

units.title: We have dozens of digital pilots but no coherent strategy

grounds.ref: South Africans are saving less as rising costs reshape priorities — FinMark Trust (FinScope Consumer SA 2025), 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows formal savings collapsed from 30% to 22% of adults in a single year and that only 15.3% of savers use liquid emergency accounts, showing that even disciplined savers routinely hold no real buffer against a shock.

grounds.ref: 66% of South Africans risk family feuds by dying without wills: Sanlam survey — TimesLIVE (Sanlam Legacy Wills Survey), 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that 66% of South Africans have no will, evidencing that most families are exposed to the intestate succession process the unit addresses.

grounds.ref: EXPLAINER | Most South Africans die without a will — News24 (citing Master of the High Court statistics), 2024
grounds.evidences: Cites Master of the High Court data showing fewer than 15% of South Africans die with a valid will, confirming that intestate succession — where the law, not the family, decides asset distribution — is the norm rather than the exception.

grounds.ref: South Africans are saving less as rising costs reshape priorities — FinMark Trust (FinScope Consumer SA 2025), 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows 48% of SA adults (22.4 million people) save nothing at all, meaning a small ordinary shock (a fare, a fee, a clinic visit) has no buffer to absorb it and becomes a crisis by default.

grounds.ref: 40,000 unregistered mashonisas operate across South Africa — AZ Big Media (Wonga research), n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents roughly 40,000 informal moneylenders charging 30-50% interest on tiny short-term loans (R50-R5,000), evidencing that people with no buffer routinely resort to costly informal borrowing for exactly the kind of small shock the unit describes.

grounds.ref: SA Ponzi schemes are miles ahead of authorities — Moneyweb, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents the scale of major South African Ponzi schemes (e.g. Mirror Trading International, BHI Trust, each losing billions of Rand to trusted-network investors) and ongoing FSCA enforcement action, evidencing that 'guaranteed high-return' schemes sold through trusted networks are a real and recurring phenomenon in South Africa.

grounds.ref: Women Drive Divorce Filings as Marriages Continue to Decline in South Africa — Statistics South Africa (Marriages and Divorces 2024), 2026
grounds.evidences: Stats SA recorded 24,202 completed divorces in 2024 (up 8.9% on 2023), with 42% of divorces in the preceding year involving unions under ten years, evidencing that division of jointly built wealth on separation is a large and growing real-world event, not a rare one.

grounds.ref: South Africa's life and disability insurance shortfall widens to R50.4 trillion — ASISA (2025 Insurance Gap Study), 2025
grounds.evidences: Finds that South Africa's 16.1 million formally employed earners collectively hold enough life and disability cover to replace only 39% of the income their families would need, evidencing that being nominally 'covered' routinely means being covered for far less than is actually required.

grounds.ref: SA Ponzi schemes are miles ahead of authorities — Moneyweb, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents multi-billion-Rand South African investment frauds (Mirror Trading International, BHI Trust) that continue despite FSCA warnings, evidencing a real basis for the fear that money placed with an investment scheme may not be safe.

grounds.ref: South Africans are saving less as rising costs reshape priorities — FinMark Trust (FinScope Consumer SA 2025), 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows only 40% of savers use organised/regulated savings channels and 13% keep cash at home, evidencing that fear of formal investment vehicles has a real behavioural counterpart in avoidance of them.

grounds.ref: Understanding Customer Concentration Risk — Subscript / industry risk analysis, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Establishes the industry benchmark that a single customer above 10-15% of revenue, or a top-five group above 25%, is flagged as a material risk by lenders and investors, evidencing that dependence on one customer a business 'can't afford to lose' is a recognised, measurable business vulnerability.

grounds.ref: The Hidden Costs of Owner Burnout in Small Businesses — EOH/EOHCB, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents that roughly 40% of a small business's success depends on the individual owner and that the owner is typically the sole 'source of action' in firms of 1-50 employees, evidencing the real structural trap of a business built entirely around one person that the unit calls 'the golden cage'.

grounds.ref: The Promise That Turned Into a Battlefield: How Business Disputes Escalate — Alismela Law, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents how partnerships based on trust rather than written agreement routinely collapse into disputes because there is no record of who contributed what or agreed to what, evidencing the real-world cost of the 'we trust each other, why write it down' assumption.

grounds.ref: Effects of physical stock loss on the financial performance of retail enterprises — Tabane, South African Journal of Economic and Management Sciences (SAJEMS), 2024
grounds.evidences: Finds that physical stock loss explains 31% of the variance in retail SME profitability and 47% of the variance in sales volume loss, with internal theft the strongest single predictor — evidencing that unexplained cash/stock leakage inside small South African businesses is a measured, significant driver of losses, not a rare fear.

grounds.ref: The Hidden Costs of Owner Burnout in Small Businesses — EOH/EOHCB, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents that South African small business owners face compounding stressors (load-shedding, rising costs, compliance burden, being the sole source of business activity) that drive high rates of stress and burnout, and that owner burnout in turn drives away high performing staff — evidencing that a business running on the owner's exhaustion is a real, documented failure pattern.

grounds.ref: New Evidence The Peter Principle Is Real - And What To Do About It — Forbes (citing Benson, Li & Shue, Univ. of Minnesota/MIT/Yale study of 53,035 sales employees, 214 firms, 2005-2011), 2018
grounds.evidences: Finds that the best-performing individual contributors are systematically the most likely to be promoted into management, and systematically perform worse as managers than their peers — evidencing that being 'the best' at one's job is a real, documented predictor of struggling once promoted, exactly the pattern the unit names.

grounds.ref: South Africa's water crisis needs R400bn to fix — The Citizen (citing Dept. of Water and Sanitation infrastructure backlog figures), 2026
grounds.evidences: Reports a national municipal water infrastructure backlog of R400 billion against annual national grant allocations of only R12.3 billion, evidencing that the 'defer, stretch, hold the tariff' pattern the unit describes is a nationwide, structurally underfunded problem, not one town's mismanagement.

grounds.ref: South Africa's nonrevenue water rising to worrying levels — Engineering News (Blue Drop/No Drop / DWS data), 2023
grounds.evidences: Documents that municipalities collectively owe water boards over R15 billion and the national department close to R20 billion, evidencing the same billed-versus-cost funding gap the unit's town faces is a widespread municipal reality.

grounds.ref: South Africa's nonrevenue water rising to worrying levels — Engineering News (Blue Drop/No Drop / DWS data), 2023
grounds.evidences: Reports national non-revenue water rising to 46.4% (from 35% in 2015), representing roughly 1,989 million cubic metres lost annually — evidencing that the '40% of pumped water never billed' problem the unit describes is the documented national pattern, and that visible-leak repair alone (the foreman's scepticism) has not moved the national number over years.

grounds.ref: South Africa's water crisis: Nearly half of treated water wasted — Sunday Independent (No Drop Report 2025), 2026
grounds.evidences: Confirms non-revenue water at 47.3% nationally with wide variation by municipality (small B4 municipalities averaging 72.5% water losses versus metros at 34.3%), evidencing this is a persistent, measured, sector-wide problem rather than an isolated plant's failure.

grounds.ref: Saving Behavior Across the Wealth Distribution — Moll et al., academic working paper, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Analyses how saving behaviour and resulting wealth trajectories diverge sharply even among households with similar income, evidencing that identical earnings can still produce very different financial outcomes for reasons other than income itself.

grounds.ref: South Africans are saving less as rising costs reshape priorities — FinMark Trust (FinScope Consumer SA 2025), 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows the 'Opportunity' (saving/investing) dimension of financial health falling from 32% to 28% of adults even as overall income levels are unchanged, evidencing that structural saving behaviour, not income level, separates who moves forward financially.

grounds.ref: The Psychology of Emotional Spending — Psychology Today, 2023
grounds.evidences: Documents emotional spending as a common, largely unexamined learned coping mechanism that provides short-term relief while creating long-term financial harm, evidencing the real psychological pattern behind money disappearing on purchases that bring no lasting satisfaction.

grounds.ref: Do consumers' post-purchase regrets reinforce or inhibit future impulse buying behavior? — Current Psychology, Springer Nature, 2025
grounds.evidences: Finds a strong positive correlation (r = 0.76) between impulsive spending and buyer's remorse, evidencing that a significant share of everyday spending is later regretted rather than valued — the exact split the unit describes between money that 'bought nothing' and money well spent.

grounds.ref: How Investment Fees Affect Returns — U.S. Department of Labor analysis, cited via Kinecta Financial Wellness Center, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Cites the U.S. Department of Labor finding that a 1% annual fee can shrink a retirement balance by up to 28% over 35 years because it compounds against the accumulated balance every period, evidencing precisely the mechanism the unit describes — a 'tiny' percentage fee quietly consuming a large share of lifetime savings.

grounds.ref: Concentration Risk: Do All Your Stock Investments Act the Same? — American Century Investments, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Explains that concentrated single-holding portfolios have historically produced greater volatility and larger downside losses than diversified portfolios over long horizons, evidencing the real risk mechanism behind losing everything by putting it all into one company one believes in, regardless of how well that company is known.

grounds.ref: South Africans are saving less as rising costs reshape priorities — FinMark Trust (FinScope Consumer SA 2025), 2025
grounds.evidences: Shows nearly half of adults have no savings buffer at all, evidencing that an ordinary shock like a broken essential tool forces a choice between damaging accumulated assets and taking on debt, because there is no third option for most people.

grounds.ref: 40,000 unregistered mashonisas operate across South Africa — AZ Big Media (Wonga research), n.d.
grounds.evidences: Documents that short-term informal credit in South Africa carries 30-50% interest, evidencing how converting a modest, one-off cash need into debt can rapidly outgrow the original problem it was meant to solve.

grounds.ref: Lusardi, A., & Mitchell, O.S. (2011). Financial Literacy around the World: An Overview. NBER Working Paper No. 17107
grounds.evidences: Lusardi and Mitchell's international research programme documents that financial illiteracy is widespread even in countries with developed financial markets, and that people with lower financial literacy make measurably worse investment and borrowing decisions, evidencing that the feeling of facing a jargon wall when investing reflects a real, widely-measured knowledge gap rather than personal inadequacy.

grounds.ref: Financial literacy in South Africa: evidence from the National Income Dynamics Study (NIDS) Wave 5, SALDRU Working Paper, University of Cape Town (2019)
grounds.evidences: Using South Africa's first nationally representative financial-literacy data (NIDS Wave 5, 2017), this SALDRU study finds financial literacy is low nationally and lowest among low-income, less-educated respondents, evidencing that the barrier facing a South African who has saved money and does not know how to invest it without guessing is a documented, measured national pattern, not an individual failing.

grounds.ref: Actively managed funds vs passive in H2 2025: SPIVA insights — Moneyweb, 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports SPIVA South Africa data showing 81-92% of actively managed South African equity funds underperformed their benchmark index over the period measured, and roughly two-thirds to three-quarters over ten years, evidencing precisely the pattern the unit describes — an expensive, actively managed fund losing to a cheap, unambitious index fund over the long run.

grounds.ref: National Treasury Republic of South Africa — Retirement Fund Reform (Discussion Paper), National Treasury, n.d.

grounds.ref: Lifestyle creep explained: Monitor spending and splurges — Empower, n.d.
grounds.evidences: Describes lifestyle inflation as a well-documented pattern in which spending rises in lockstep with income, leaving households no financially better off despite earning substantially more — evidencing exactly the stagnation-despite-raises the unit describes.

grounds.ref: 10X Investments Retirement Reality Report 2023/2024 (citing National Treasury data) — Moneyweb, 2024
grounds.evidences: Confirms that only 6% of South Africans on ordinary salaries are on track to retire comfortably, showing that the outcome this unit describes (an ordinary earner reaching financial independence) is genuinely rare and that the learner's scepticism reflects a real, widespread failure to achieve it, not a personal deficiency.

grounds.ref: One-More-Year Syndrome in FIRE: Causes, FOMO and How to Stop Delaying — The Good Life Journey, 2026
grounds.evidences: Documents 'One-More-Year Syndrome' as a recognised, recurring pattern among people who have already reached financial independence yet keep working, rooted in loss aversion and scarcity-honed habits that do not switch off — evidencing that the unit's exact phenomenon (arrival without ability to stop) is a real, named problem, not a rare quirk.

grounds.ref: South African households have a R2.4 trillion problem — BusinessTech, 2025 (National Credit Regulator data)
grounds.evidences: Shows that South African household debt has reached R2.4 trillion with 4.9 million consumers holding impaired credit records and 6.3 million in early-stage arrears, evidencing that the trap of judging affordability by a small periodic instalment rather than the true total cost is producing real, large-scale financial harm.

grounds.ref: Deming & Silliman (2024). Skills and Human Capital in the Labor Market — review (EconStor)
grounds.evidences: The Mincer human-capital earnings model, one of the most replicated results in labour economics, shows that wages are a function of accumulated skill and experience rather than hours worked alone, and recent extensions show returns to skill (including noncognitive skill) rising over time, evidencing that an hour's worth is not fixed but is measurably raised by the skill embodied in it.

grounds.ref: SA tops global fraud charts as FSCA flags social media investment scams — Moonstone Information Refinery, 2025
grounds.evidences: Reports that 68% of South Africans were targeted by fraud attempts between August and December 2024, that 37.5% of finance-related social media ads analysed were scams, and that digital fraud losses rose from R1bn to R1.4bn in a year — evidencing that the fast-talking 'flip your money' stranger-investment approach this unit warns against is a real, currently escalating threat, not a hypothetical one.

grounds.ref: A systematic review and meta-analysis of compassion fatigue among healthcare professionals before and during COVID-19 in Sub-Saharan Africa — PMC, 2024
grounds.evidences: Finds that roughly three in four healthcare and caregiving professionals across Southern/Sub-Saharan Africa experience compassion fatigue, evidencing that giving from a depleted position — the unit's core problem — produces measurable, widespread exhaustion and reduced capacity to help, rather than being an isolated personal failing.

grounds.ref: Foreign aid advances donors' interests and creates dependency — Africa at LSE (LSE Blogs), 2025
grounds.evidences: Documents that repeated direct aid/assistance ('giving fish' rather than 'equipping to fish') measurably fuels a dependency syndrome and erodes recipients' self-reliant capacity — evidencing that the unit's core claim, that consumable help repeated without building capacity fails to reduce future need, is a documented real-world pattern, not just an individual family's experience.

grounds.evidences: Documents, via Little's Law, that large batches spend measurably more time waiting in queues between process steps than small batches moving through a pull system, and that this drives up the time customers/service-recipients wait — evidencing that the unit's counter-intuitive claim (making everything in one large go, while cheaper per item, worsens the wait experienced by the people served) reflects an established operations-management finding.

grounds.evidences: Ryan and Deci's foundational, empirically-tested theory establishes competence (alongside autonomy and relatedness) as one of three basic psychological needs whose satisfaction is required for motivation and well-being, evidencing that the felt gap between caring about work and not yet being competent at it is a documented psychological reality, not just self-doubt.

grounds.ref: Ericsson, K.A., & Harwell, K.W. (2019). Deliberate Practice and Proposed Limits on the Effects of Practice on the Acquisition of Expert Performance. Frontiers in Psychology, 10:2396
grounds.evidences: Building on Ericsson's original deliberate-practice research programme, this paper documents that expert-level performance is acquired only through sustained, structured practice with feedback over time, not simply by trying or caring, evidencing that the novice-to-trusted-practitioner gap in the unit's problem is a real, well-studied developmental process with no shortcut.
